blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A depot model's HiGHS log shows Matrix [1e-02, 1e+09] and Cost [1e+00, 5e+03], and no WARNING lines at all. A reviewer says the model is well scaled because HiGHS did not warn. What do you answer?

options.text: Agree, since HiGHS warns about every range that is outside its limits
options.says: HiGHS warned about the colleague's costs and said nothing about the 1e9 in the same model's matrix.

options.text: Agree, since a wide matrix span is harmless when the costs are small
options.says: The span is a problem on its own: the guidelines put the limit at 1e9, and a huge coefficient turns tolerances into room.

options.text: Disagree, since the matrix spans eleven powers of ten whatever the log says
options.says: Right: the ranges are the measure; a model without warnings is not a well-scaled model.

options.text: Disagree, since any model whose costs exceed 1,000 needs rescaling
options.says: Costs up to a few thousand are well within the guidelines; the tight GridCap model has them.

origin.section: A Model Written in Mixed Units Spreads Its Numbers Over Many Powers of Ten

questions.stem: A water model measures a tank's fill in litres. You switch the variable to kilolitres, so fill = 1000 * fill_kl. What happens to the numbers of that column?

options.text: Its coefficients grow 1,000 times, and its bounds shrink 1,000 times
options.says: Right: substituting fill = 1000 * fill_kl multiplies its coefficients by 1,000 and divides its bounds by 1,000.

options.text: Its coefficients shrink 1,000 times, and its bounds grow 1,000 times
options.says: That is the opposite substitution, kilolitres to litres.

options.text: Its coefficients and bounds stay the same, and only the report changes
options.says: A column scaling changes its coefficients and its bounds; the plan is what stays.

options.text: Every right-hand side grows 1,000 times, and so the best plan changes
options.says: Scaling a column touches only that column; the allowed plans and the best plan stay the same.

origin.section: Rescaling Multiplies a Row, a Column or the Objective, and Leaves the Plan Unchanged

questions.stem: A model has costs up to 4e7 and a big-M of 1e9 in one row. HiGHS's log suggests setting user_objective_scale to -5, and you do. What changes in the next solve?

options.text: The 1e9 is scaled down as well, since the option rescales the whole model
options.says: After the option was set, the log's Matrix line still read [1e-01, 1e+09].

options.text: The objective comes back 32 times smaller, since HiGHS keeps the scaled value
options.says: HiGHS reports the unscaled objective, and MathOpt returned the same 23,161,500 as before.

options.text: The plan can change, since scaling the objective changes which plans are best
options.says: Multiplying the objective by a positive number keeps the same best plans.

options.text: The cost warning stops, though the matrix still holds the 1e9 coefficient
options.says: Right: the costs were scaled by a power of two; no option removes the big-M from the matrix.

origin.section: HiGHS Can Scale the Objective and Bounds for You, Not the Matrix
